NDT ERP in Vernon, California: software for a market made of many small jobs

An NDT ERP for Vernon has to handle volume, not size. The city is 5.2 square miles of almost entirely industrial land southeast of downtown Los Angeles, with more than 1,800 businesses and tens of thousands of daily workers, so an inspection company working here runs a high count of short jobs for many different clients. The software has to make each of those jobs cheap to quote, staff, report and bill.

That is a different problem from the one a refinery-turnaround contractor has. A turnaround contractor worries about mobilising sixty technicians for six weeks. A Vernon-focused contractor worries about the fourteen separate half-day call-outs this week, each with its own purchase order, site contact, safety induction and report format, and each one easy to lose money on if the paperwork costs more than the inspection. The Atlantis ERP solution is a fully customized ERP for NDT and inspection companies, set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder Anoop Rayavarapu is an ASNT NDT Level III. It is affordable, accessible and fully customizable, and the rest of this section explains what that means for a company whose book of work is spread across Vernon's industrial grid and the refineries, ports and fabricators around it.

If you already know your pain points, skip straight to a conversation: book a demo configured for Vernon work.

What is the best NDT software for inspection companies working Vernon's industrial tenants?

The best NDT software for this market is the one that keeps per-job overhead low while holding the evidence clients audit: technician certificates, instrument calibration and a signed report tied to the job. For a company serving many small tenants, that means quoting, dispatch, reporting and invoicing in one system, not four.

Vernon's client base is mixed. Food and beverage processors run ammonia refrigeration, pressure vessels and stainless process piping. Metal fabricators, plating and finishing shops and machinery builders need weld examination on structural and pressure work. The city-owned Malburg Generating Station, a natural-gas combined-cycle plant that has been in commercial operation since 2005 and is run by Vernon Public Utilities, brings boiler, HRSG and piping work of a more traditional power-plant kind. And large parcels are being redeveloped, including the former Farmer John meatpacking site, which closed in early 2023 after more than ninety years and was bought by an industrial property developer. Redevelopment means new construction steel, and new construction means weld inspection.

No single report template or pricing model covers all of that. What the software must do is let one crew move between those clients in a week without anyone retyping data, and let the owner see which client types actually make money. That is the test to apply to any NDT inspection software you shortlist, including ours.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for half-day call-outs

When jobs are short, the quote and the invoice are a large share of the admin cost, so they need to be fast and consistent. In the Atlantis ERP, quotes carry the job type, site, project dates and the applicable codes; your NDT services are set up as products flagged with method and category, so a quote for MT on a fabricator's weldments or UT thickness on a food plant's vessel is built from lines you have already defined. A global discount can be applied for a standing-agreement client. The quotation PDF is branded to your company, and the client can accept and sign online, which converts the quote into a sales order without anyone re-entering it.

Invoices carry the NDT project, the client's job or PO number, the site, the invoice type and the industry sector, and they subtotal labour, equipment and consumables separately. Each invoice line can carry a cost centre, the method, the equipment serial number used, the technician, the rate type and the days or hours. That level of detail matters in Vernon because many tenants are subsidiaries of larger groups whose accounts-payable teams reject invoices that do not match the PO line for line.

Timesheet hours feed billing directly. Each entry has a work type (inspection, travel, standby or setup), a billable flag and a rate multiplier, so the standby hour spent waiting for a lockout-tagout release at a food plant is recorded and billed according to your agreement rather than forgotten. Payments, reminders and taxes are standard functions configured for California during implementation.

Technician certification tracking software for crews that cover the whole basin

Technician certification tracking in the Atlantis ERP records each certificate by scheme, level, method, certifying body and dates, and computes its status automatically: active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked. Schemes covered include SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP and others, and each record can hold OJT hours, training hours, exam results and attachments.

A Vernon-based technician may work a food plant in the morning, a fabricator in the afternoon and a refinery in Carson or Torrance later in the week. Each of those clients may ask for proof of qualification before site access. When the evidence lives in one record per technician, anyone in the office can pull it in seconds instead of hunting through a shared drive.

Vision tests are tracked alongside the certificates: near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception and contrast, with examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry. Examination sheets hold general, specific and practical scores against a passing score (70 percent by default, adjustable per template). The employee's NDT profile shows the highest level held, the methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry.

The system creates warning tasks 90 days before a certificate or vision test expires, and configurable daily email alerts go to the people you choose, with your own look-ahead days and resend interval. Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid, which catches the case where someone books hours on a method they are no longer current in. See the certificates app for the full record layout.

Calibration management software when one instrument serves many clients

Calibration management in the Atlantis ERP ties every instrument, probe and related item to a serial number with a calibration frequency, status and full calibration record. When one flaw detector goes to six clients in a fortnight, every report it touched depends on that record being right.

Each calibration record captures the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, whether the lab is accredited, the result (pass, fail or conditional) and the next due date. A separate calibration certificate register holds the lab's accreditation number, the certificate PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status, with expiry alerts. Purchasing can flag vendors as OEM, dealer or calibration lab, record their accreditation number and expiry, and link purchase order lines to a specific equipment serial, so the cost of sending a gauge out for calibration lands against the right instrument.

Equipment moves through an issue and return workflow with supervisor and manager approval, and its condition is recorded on the way out and on the way back. Reservations prevent two crews booking the same instrument, and the team assignment screen warns when assigned equipment is out of calibration. Consumables such as couplant, penetrant and developer, magnetic particles and PPE are tracked with reorder levels and a low-stock flag, which matters when your van is doing four PT jobs in a day. The asset management app covers this in detail.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for a dense industrial grid

Crew dispatch in the Atlantis ERP runs each job as a team assignment that moves through planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed. Double-booking of technicians and of equipment serial numbers is blocked, and each job carries site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates.

In Vernon the distances are short but the number of stops is high. A dispatcher needs to see, for each technician, current status, current assignment, utilisation and next available date, and needs a calendar that already knows who is on leave, in training, off sick or unavailable. The technician availability calendar holds exactly those states and blocks overlaps; time off requests feed it automatically. Calendar, kanban and list views let the dispatcher work the way they prefer.

Projects hold the NDT job type, site, client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope and acceptance criteria, plus the assigned equipment and technicians, job status, and fields for safety induction and work permit. That last pair is not a small thing here: food processors and the power station each run their own induction and permit systems, and a technician turned away at the gate for a missing induction is a lost half-day. Tasks under a project carry the method, technician, component, result, indication and defect counts, and procedure and WPS references. The fleet app records whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources, its transport licence number and expiry, and which job and driver it is assigned to, with dates and mileage. See team assignments.

NDT reporting software that fits food plants, fabricators and the power station

NDT reporting in the Atlantis ERP supports 17 report types, each with its own numbering: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday and coating, and computed radiography. Reports move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures.

That range matters in a mixed market. A stainless food-processing line may call for PMI and ferrite readings. A fabricator's structural steel needs VT and MT or UT on welds, with weld and job lines recording defect type and orientation. The power station's HRSG and piping work may need UT thickness readings by direction, hardness and PWHT records. Each method holds its own data: UT with a probe calibration table, RT with source, technique, IQI type and placement, MT with technique and particle type, PT with method and developer, and PAUT with focal laws. Every report records the work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing, procedure and standard references, and closes with an overall result of acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. Where a client has an authorised or third-party inspector, that name and signature are captured on the report.

Company templates are versioned and can be Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with your logo, header and footer. Excel templates are filled automatically by mapping fields to cells, so a client who insists on its own spreadsheet format still gets it without retyping. Technicians capture data in the offline field app, an installable web app that works without signal, stores drafts and photos locally and syncs later. It has a method picker, photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview. Read more on the Digital Twin Reporting Software page.

Procedures under control: one written practice, many client requirements

The procedure register holds document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and the body text or an uploaded file. Procedures move from draft to submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejection and archiving, and approved revisions are locked.

For a company serving many different clients, the procedure library tends to grow client-specific variants. A food processor's quality team may want a PT procedure that specifies a particular cleaner compatible with its sanitation programme; a fabricator building to AWS D1.1 needs a VT and UT procedure that references that code's acceptance criteria. The register records who prepared, reviewed and approved each revision and when, and keeps a snapshot of every revision so you can show exactly which text was in force on the day a job was done.

An AI-assisted first draft can be generated for a new procedure (with a built-in template as fallback), which saves the Level III from starting with a blank page. The Level III still reviews and approves; the software does not replace that judgement. Approvers get email notifications and reminders for pending approvals, so a procedure does not sit unsigned while a client waits. Details are on the procedures app page.

Spreadsheets are cheap until the first client audit. A generic ERP handles accounts well but leaves NDT records to be bolted on. The Atlantis ERP starts from NDT records and includes the business apps around them. For more, read NDT ERP vs generic ERP.

ERP for small NDT companies in the Vernon area: how implementation runs

An ERP for a small NDT company should go live in stages, starting where the pain is sharpest, and should not need an IT person on staff. For most Vernon-area companies that first stage is certificates, calibration and quoting, because those three touch every job.

A typical sequence looks like this:

  1. Discovery. We look at your current spreadsheets, report forms, written practice and invoice layouts, and list which clients have their own formats.
  2. Core records. Technicians, certificates, vision tests, instruments and calibration history are loaded, so the status of every person and every gauge is visible from day one.
  3. Quoting and projects. Your service lines are set up as NDT service products, and a project structure is configured with the induction and permit fields your clients require.
  4. Reporting. Report templates for your most common methods are configured, including any client Excel formats mapped field to cell.
  5. Billing and dashboards. Timesheets, invoice layout and the financial dashboard are switched on, and taxes and payment terms are configured for California.

Items not built in, such as a client-specific approval step, are configured during implementation. If you want to see how that would look for your company, ask for a scoped implementation plan.

Dashboards, CRM and integrations: what the owner sees on Monday

The owner of a Vernon inspection company needs three answers every Monday: who is expiring, what equipment is due or overdue, and which jobs made money. The dashboards cover certificates expiring or expired, equipment calibration due or overdue and issued equipment overdue for return. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over a 12-month view.

On the sales side, CRM leads carry service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, and each lead gets an NDT lead score from 0 to 100 grouped as hot, warm, nurture or cold. Leads can be imported from CSV, and a business card photographed at a trade event is read by AI or OCR into name, company, title, email, phones and website, then turned into a CRM lead with one click. Drip email sequences by service line can be paused, resumed or unsubscribed, which is useful when you are slowly building standing agreements with the many tenants in the city.

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. That matters when a large tenant wants inspection data pushed into its own maintenance system, or when your accountant wants to stay on QuickBooks. Companion products sit alongside: Atlantis Digital Twins for 3D visualisation of inspection data with indication mapping and thickness trends, and Practical NDT, a 3D simulator for practice. Training at Atlantis NDT is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based; see training.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Atlantis ERP affordable for a five-technician company in Vernon?

Yes, that is who it is set up for as much as larger firms. Pricing is by quote on request and depends on scope, users and integrations, and the whole suite of business apps is included rather than sold one module at a time.

Can it produce reports in a food processor's own spreadsheet format?

Yes. Excel templates are filled automatically by mapping report fields to the client's cells, and templates are versioned, so each client format stays under control.

Does the field app work inside a cold store or a basement plant room with no signal?

Yes. The offline field app stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs when it reconnects, with photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview available offline.

Will it stop a technician being sent out on an expired certificate?

It warns 90 days ahead through tasks and email alerts, marks the certificate expired on the day, and timesheets warn if hours are booked while the certificate is not valid. Double-booking of technicians and equipment is blocked outright.

Can we keep QuickBooks for accounting?

Yes. The ERP has an open REST API and integrates with QuickBooks and other systems that accept API connections, with the scope agreed during implementation.

Does Atlantis offer training for our technicians?

Atlantis NDT offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training. The ERP can record other certificates your technicians hold, such as ISO 9712, PCN or CSWIP, but Atlantis does not deliver those schemes.

How do we start?

Send us your current certificate list, one sample report and one sample invoice, and we will show you them inside the system. Request a quote for Vernon.
